passes_when: two builds of the same tree give the same root
fails_when: root construction is order-dependent or nondeterministic

passes_when: build order and verify order produce the same root
fails_when: they disagree on an intact bundle
negative_control: v1 hashed in walk order vs sorted order - this test pinned it

passes_when: an added file is reported and exit is non-zero
fails_when: an addition passes - a content-only checksum list would miss it

passes_when: a rename is reported as both ADDED and REMOVED
a missing manifest is a failure
fails_when: absence of provenance reports success - v1 printed a note and exited 0
negative_control: manifest path that does not exist (EXECUTED)

passes_when: a root header that disagrees with the observed root fails
fails_when: the root is decorative - v1 returned exit 0 and FREEZE INTACT on an all-zero root
negative_control: all-zero expected root over genuine rows (EXECUTED)

passes_when: editing the manifest is caught by its detached sidecar
fails_when: the manifest can be rewritten to match a mutated bundle

passes_when: a caller-supplied expected root is enforced
fails_when: the caller's pinned root is ignored
positive_control: F1 verify with no expected root

passes_when: a locked bundle refuses file creation, deletion and rename
fails_when: chmod on files alone - v1 left directories 775, so add/delete/replace still worked

passes_when: a stray .pyc is an ADDED file, not an invisible one
fails_when: __pycache__ is excluded from the manifest, so bytecode writes go unnoticed (v1)
